These may involve structural tank ruptures or BLEVEs triggered by external mechanical impacts, such as collisions or seismic activity, or the failure of safety systems such as TPRDs or rupture discs due to ice or debris which create the circumstances for a possible tank rupture indoors since tank pressure cannot be safely relieved. Consequences with associated risk metrics of 15 are largely driven by thermal and operational deviations during maintenance procedures. Hot work, such as welding or grinding, can both lead to an overpressurization of the fuel system and serve as an immediate ignition source for any unintended emissions of hydrogen. Moreover, the defueling process can present some risks of hydrogen release if not performed correctly. This highlights a significant reliance on human factors during the defueling process. Operational errors, including the accidental opening of manual valves without proper venting tools or the failure to confirm that hydrogen has been evacuated from a line before beginning valve maintenance, can contribute to maintenance risk. This suggests the importance of maintenance protocols and atmospheric monitoring where leaked hydrogen may accumulate. Other scenarios are associated with latent equipment degradation and instrumentation errors that compromise the defueling process. Water, corrosive cleaning agents, or de-icing salts may seize safety components such as TPRDs over time, possibly resulting in a high-pressure release. Lower rated risk scenarios involve chronic integrity failures and localized leaks of components like gaskets, seals, and valves. They are categorized as lower risk because the resulting slow leaks typically involve lower mass-flow rates that are more easily managed by the facility’s active ventilation system. Such preventative measures such as a ventilation systems can help disperse hydrogen, lowering the probability of accumulation and subsequent explosion [26]. Another risk includes the failure of check valves which may allow air or moisture into the system which can lead to internal degradation or unpredictable combustion during subsequent operations.
